title: Kusto Query Language (KQL) for Developers
description: Learn KQL basics to query logs, filter events, and aggregate data in Log Analytics.

data.text: Kusto Query Language (KQL) is the query language used to retrieve data from Azure Monitor logs. It is a read-only query language similar to SQL but optimized for exploring large volumes of log data. KQL is also used in Azure Data Explorer and Microsoft 365 Defender.

terms.definition: A structured set of rows, such as AppRequests or Syslog.
A named field within a table, such as TimeGenerated or Message.
A keyword that transforms data, such as where, extend, summarize, or join.
The pipe operator passes results from one operator to the next.

data.title: Operators Every Developer Should Know
items: where: Filter rows by a condition.
project / extend: Select or add columns.
summarize: Aggregate data (count, avg, max, min).
order by / top: Sort results and limit output.
join: Combine data from two tables.
make-series: Create time-series data for charts.

data.title: Aggregate Request Count by Hour
data.content: Count failed requests per hour over the last 24 hours:
data.code:
AppRequests
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where Success == false
| summarize FailedRequests = count() by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| order by TimeGenerated asc

data.title: Join App Requests with Exceptions (KQL)
data.content: Find requests that resulted in exceptions:
data.code:
let failedRequests = AppRequests
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where Success == false
| project OperationId, Name, ResultCode;
failedRequests
| join kind=inner (
    Exceptions
    | project OperationId, Type, Message
) on OperationId

data.title: Use IntelliSense in the Portal
data.text: The Log Analytics query editor in the Azure Portal includes IntelliSense, schema browsing, and time-range pickers. Start there to explore available tables and columns before writing complex queries.
